the_defect_this_points_at.current_correction: the contract now scopes what to do first to three named situations -- fresh implementation with the file absent orders the skeleton first; a RESUMED correction reads and PRESERVES its existing document and corrects it in place; the REVIEWER writes no part of it -- with the same criteria, the same single-file scope and the same 180-second cap for both roles. Review 314389 R1 required that scoping: the unconditional order told the reviewer to write the proposal and told a restored implementer to discard its own correction.
the_defect_this_points_at.hypothesis: the task document told the worker WHAT to write and WHAT WOULD BE ACCEPTED and never told it the turn was BOUNDED, and an agent that does not know it is on a clock reads until the clock ends. This is a HYPOTHESIS the observations support, not a demonstrated cause.
the_defect_this_points_at.not_the_timeout: the cap is untouched. What would justify raising it is a session that wrote the file early and was still improving it when the cap stopped it. Neither measured session was that.
the_defect_this_points_at.proposed_experiment: change that one thing and measure the next session the same way. NEXT-EXPERIMENT-314263-SECOND.json carries it; it has NOT been run and is not authorized here.
the_defect_this_points_at.superseded_first_attempt: AN EARLIER VERSION OF THIS CORRECTION stated the bound and asked for the file 'within the first quarter of the turn'. That text is SUPERSEDED: the interrupted session ran under it and spent its first 51.6 seconds reading with nothing written (INTERRUPTED-RUN-314263.json).
the_defect_this_points_at.verified: focused deterministic cases per situation in test_correction_packet.py. They are STRING assertions over a generated document: they prove the contract says these things, not that a model obeys them.

what_the_provider_actually_did.prompt_first_line: Write docs/v12-context-correction.md -- an operator guide for the managed context-correction workflow
what_the_provider_actually_did.reading_not_thrashing: the 47 commands are 47 DIFFERENT reads -- ls, grep, sed, cat, wc over the checkout -- with no repetition and no error loop. The worker was making steady progress at understanding, and had produced nothing to deliver.

what_these_measurements_do_not_establish.no_causation: nothing here proves the missing time reminder CAUSED the failure; it shows a session that read continuously and wrote nothing under a contract that never mentioned the bound
what_these_measurements_do_not_establish.no_guarantee_from_the_fix: writing an early skeleton does not guarantee completion within 180 seconds, and an early skeleton is not acceptance
what_these_measurements_do_not_establish.no_partition_of_latency: the transcript does not partition model or service latency from tool execution inside the session span
what_these_measurements_do_not_establish.one_session_each: two sessions, one of them interrupted at 51.6 seconds. Two runs are not a distribution.

where_the_time_went.how_the_residual_was_computed: serving_seconds_spent minus the transcript span minus the startup interval. It is an ATTRIBUTION BY SUBTRACTION, not directly measured exclusive manager execution: anything happening inside that window that the transcript does not timestamp falls into it.
where_the_time_went.verdict: OBSERVED: the prompt arrived, the session ran 172.4 seconds, made 47 reads and produced no deliverable. NOT ESTABLISHED by these numbers: which part was model latency, which was tool execution, or that the absent time reminder CAUSED the failure. The manager-overhead figure is a residual. Provider delay and manager overhead are not RULED OUT by arithmetic -- they are bounded by it: neither can exceed the small intervals outside the session span.
where_the_time_went.what_is_INFERRED: that the session span is time the provider spent working rather than waiting. The transcript timestamps entries, not the split between model latency, service queueing and tool execution, so this measurement does NOT partition those.
